rationale:
bugs_open/308: the misdirected_cta detector and the CTA repairer answer 'which pages may be a CTA destination?' from different sources, so 200 findings (re-measured live 2026-08-22, up from the filed 149) name a repair no writer can perform. 112 of them sit on work items the platform marked COMPLETE — the repair ran, reported success and changed nothing.

The blocker is that CTA provenance is DERIVED, not recorded (LNK-033): 'no resolver path can produce a utility-area destination, therefore a stored valid one was authored'. Fixing 308 means letting labels resolve INTO utility pages, which falsifies that invariant directly — and then both of bugs_open/248's keep-branches would freeze the resolver's own output, with the detector arm that would have noticed already demoted. The OWNER RULED on 2026-08-18 (recorded in the bug file): build the real provenance record — fix candidate 1 — provenance FIRST, then the widening; and no opt-out flags.

THIS SUBMISSION IS PHASE A ONLY: record the provenance and re-base the predicate on it. It is behaviour-preserving by construction — with zero stamps in the DB and today's narrow candidate set the resolver never mints a utility url, so the new conjunct never fires. PHASE B (deleting candidatesFromHubs' filter, one shared candidate universe for detector and repairer, stopword recalibration, and a completion verifier) is a SEPARATE submission gated on this one being pod-verified live. I am naming it here rather than letting a reviewer discover it: Phase B retires LNK-033's invariant deliberately, and that retirement is the owner's 2026-08-18 ruling, not this lane's choice. Per the 2026-07-29 ruling I claim NO ordering constraint — I could not hold this out of the fleet if I wanted to.

Design pivot worth reviewing hardest: the stamp is VALUE-BOUND (it records WHICH url was minted, per field, not a boolean). That is what makes 8 of RFC_042's 9 content_data writers correct with zero code changes, and it is the only version that survives the section-editor MERGE case — under a boolean stamp a surviving stamp would licence the recompute to clobber a human's edit, which is bugs_open/248 all over again.

plan.summary: Record CTA destination provenance as a value-bound reserved key in page_components.content_data (__cta_minted: {url_field: minted_url}), written by BOTH resolver writers on every branch that writes a url AND at setCTAField's unresolved fallthrough; re-base storedCTADestinationIsAuthored on it by changing its SIGNATURE so no caller can use the shape test without the mint check. No config key, no migration, no backfill: an absent stamp preserves today's exact semantics.

edits.rationale: The provenance vocabulary, in datahelpers because BOTH writers (actions package) and any future check need it, and because actions imports datahelpers but not vice versa — the same placement reason links_tel.go (LNK-034) and ctafields.go already use. Pure functions, no DB, no config surface at all: per the owner's 'no opt-out flags' ruling there is nothing here a caller can switch off. Comparison is via NormalizePagePath so /contact.html and /contact/index.html cannot disagree — the same normaliser the keeps and the detector already share.

Re-base the predicate on the record. The SIGNATURE change is the enforcement, not decoration: taking (stored, field) instead of a bare url means no caller can reach the utility-area shape test without also passing the map the mint check reads. A caller that only has a url string will not compile — which is the compile-time version of 'a comment is not a control on a tree this many sessions share' (owner, 2026-08-02). Validity stays load-bearing: an INVALID /contact.html is bugs_open/203's phantom and replacing it is the repair, pinned by an existing test.

Stamp on every branch that WRITES a url (label match, authored-utility keep, non-page keep, positional pick) — a keep re-asserts the provenance it already had, which is why the keeps stamp too rather than only the fresh picks. AND re-stamp at the UNRESOLVED FALLTHROUGH: that branch writes nothing to resolved[field], so whatever plan_sections' PBP-039 carry left there is persisted, and the plan->save funnel is DELETE+INSERT (RFC_042 §2) so the previous cycle's stamp is NOT preserved by the persist. Without this, a resolver-minted url that goes through the carry arrives unstamped next cycle, reads as authored and is frozen — 308's own failure mode reintroduced through its fix. Note the fix is HERE and not in carryStored: setCTAField is handed `stored` as a FRESH page_components read (loadExistingSectionContentData, call site :207-212), not the carry's output, so the stamp is already in hand and PBP-039's carry — whose register entry says do not remove it, do not reorder it — is untouched.
edits.sketch:
@@ setCTAField, label-match branch @@
 			resolved[field] = match.URL
+			datahelpers.SetCTAMinted(resolved, field, match.URL)
@@ setCTAField, bugs_open/248 authored-utility keep @@
 		resolved[field] = storedURL
+		// keeps re-assert provenance: if the stamp covered this value it still
+		// does, and if it did not this stays authored.
+		if datahelpers.CTAMintedCovers(stored, field, storedURL) {
+			datahelpers.SetCTAMinted(resolved, field, storedURL)
+		}
@@ setCTAField, positional pick @@
 		resolved[field] = target.URL
+		datahelpers.SetCTAMinted(resolved, field, target.URL)
@@ setCTAField, unresolved fallthrough (writes nothing today) @@
+	// The carry (PBP-039) may have left a previously-minted url in resolved
+	// [field]; the save REPLACES content_data, so an unstamped survivor reads
+	// authored next cycle and freezes. Re-assert what the stored row records.
+	if carried, _ := resolved[field].(string); carried != "" &&
+		datahelpers.CTAMintedCovers(stored, field, carried) {
+		datahelpers.SetCTAMinted(resolved, field, carried)
+	}
 	*unresolved = append(*unresolved, map[string]interface{}{

edits.rationale: The repair-path writer, kept in lockstep with the build-path one — they are two writers of one field and 248 was caused by only one of them being fixed. KEEP #1 consumes the new predicate. KEEP #2 and KEEP #3 and THEIR ORDER ARE UNTOUCHED: KEEP #3 (LNK-034, tel:/mailto:) is reachable only because KEEP #2 requires validPages.Contains, an ordering that is mutation-proven and documented in place, and nothing here needs to disturb it. KEEP #2's non-utility values are not stamped by this change (they may be authored ordinary links; stamping them would assert provenance this change has no evidence for) — stated explicitly because it is the asymmetry a reviewer should push on.
edits.sketch:
@@ applyCTARecompute, label-match branch @@
 			resolved[field] = match.URL
+			datahelpers.SetCTAMinted(resolved, field, match.URL)
@@ applyCTARecompute, KEEP #1 @@
-	if hasCurrent && storedCTADestinationIsAuthored(current, validPages) &&
+	if hasCurrent && storedCTADestinationIsAuthored(stored, field, validPages) &&
 		datahelpers.NormalizePagePath(current) != datahelpers.NormalizePagePath(pageURL) {
@@ applyCTARecompute, positional pick @@
 	resolved[field] = target.URL
+	datahelpers.SetCTAMinted(resolved, field, target.URL)

edits.rationale: Unit-pins the value-binding, which is the design's load-bearing property. Includes the normalisation boundary (/contact.html vs /contact/index.html must be the SAME value) and the absent-stamp default (false — the no-backfill guarantee). MUTATION PROOF: make CTAMintedCovers presence-bound (ignore the url) and TestStaleStampDoesNotCoverEditedValue fails — that is the section-editor clobber.

The asymmetry pin is UNCHANGED in this phase — bugs_open/308's verification bar #2 says that if that test is edited without provenance landing, the fix is wrong, so it stays byte-identical here and is rewritten only in Phase B, after the stamp is pod-verified. Its call sites are updated for the new signature only. New cases: a minted utility destination is RE-DERIVABLE (mutation: drop the !CTAMintedCovers conjunct -> this fails, and it is the LNK-033 landmine as a test); an unstamped stored utility url is still KEPT (248 unregressed); a carried value at the unresolved fallthrough keeps its stamp (mutation: delete the fallthrough re-stamp -> this fails).

grounded_in: bugs_open/308 OWNER RULINGS 2026-08-18: 'Build the provenance record. Fix candidate 1 is the chosen route.' and 'No opt-out flags. Don't add any new flags that let other agents ignore things — this leads to bugs.'

Re-measured live 2026-08-22: the bug file's own query returns 200 findings (filed at 149 on 2026-08-17), split complete 71 items/112 findings, unresolved 53/86, cancelled 2/2 — the 112 are repairs that ran, reported success and changed nothing.

DEMAND CONTROL, same day: SELECT date_trunc('day',created_at), count(*) FROM site_work_items WHERE item_key LIKE 'misdirected_cta:%' returns 2026-08-19: 3, 08-18: 128, 08-17: 208 — the detector has been silent for three days, so 200 is a STOCK not a flow and no post-fix count is evidence until a discovery run is induced.

resolve_internal_links_action.go:674-676 (storedCTADestinationIsAuthored) — 'THE INVARIANT: no resolver path can produce a utility-area destination... A stored url that is BOTH a valid page AND in a utility area was therefore not written by setCTAField or applyCTARecompute.' This is the derived provenance being replaced.

The design's load-bearing assumption MEASURED, not assumed, and grouped so it could have come out otherwise: 16 rows across FOUR component functions (content-block-about 12, gauntlet-cta 2, archetype-combinations 1, archetype-grid 1) store a *_target_title key their input_schema does NOT declare (bool_or over content_components.input_schema = f). Counting the 844 total would have proven nothing — 438 sit on hero/call-to-action, which DO declare it. So an undeclared resolver key survives into stored content_data.

The __ namespace is clean fleet-wide: SELECT jsonb_object_keys over page_components.content_data LIKE '\_\_%' returns 0 rows (underscores escaped — unescaped, _ is a LIKE wildcard and the query returns every key).

resolve_internal_links_action.go:207-212 — setCTAField is handed `existing` from loadExistingSectionContentData, a FRESH page_components read, while the PBP-039 carry's output is the separate `resolved` argument. This is why the stamp fix belongs in setCTAField and PBP-039's carry is untouched.

setCTAField's final branch appends to *unresolved and writes NOTHING to resolved[field]; every other branch assigns it. RFC_042 §2 records the plan->save funnel as DELETE+INSERT (REPLACE), so a carried value surviving that branch is persisted without the previous cycle's stamp.

rerender_page_sections_action.go:1057-1065 — '⚠ THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: this branch is reachable only because keep #2's predicate requires validPages.Contains'. KEEP #2/#3 and their order are deliberately untouched by this change.

Consumer enumeration by symbol sweep (not assertion): loadContentHubs/loadInteractivePages have THREE non-test callers — resolve_internal_links_action.go, rerender_page_sections_action.go, and render_site_components_action.go:182-190 (the site HEADER CTA fallback), which no CTA bug file or register entry names. Phase B therefore widens at the candidate-assembly seam and NOT at the loaders; site_components stores 0 cta_url keys across all 24 header rows, so a content_data diff could not have seen a header regression.
plan.risks:
1) FREEZE RESIDUAL: any path that carries a minted value forward without its stamp yields a false 'authored' and freezes that link. Mitigated at the one known site (setCTAField's unresolved fallthrough) and safe by direction elsewhere — the frozen value is a valid page and the label-match branch still runs AHEAD of every keep in both writers, so a frozen link whose copy names another page is still repaired. Disconfirming observation: a page_component_history pair where a utility-valid field was stamped in generation N and unstamped-same-value in N+1.
2) The stamp reaching rendered HTML or a writer prompt. Disconfirming observation: fleet grep of rendered_html for __cta_minted must return 0 after Phase A rolls. [ASSUMED] no template ranges over content_data keys.
3) The RFC_042/355 content-loss lane later widens its differ to all keys and reads stamp churn as key loss. Prevented by the stamp being deliberately NOT schema-declared (their differ is scoped to schema-declared non-LLM keys) plus a CONTRIB into their NOTES naming the reserved key. Disconfirming observation: their next run files a __cta_minted finding.
4) [UNVERIFIED] I have not read the function that folds resolved_data into persisted content_data; the measurement in grounded_in proves the OUTCOME (undeclared keys arrive) without my having read the writer. Owed before merge.
5) Phase B, NOT in this submission, retires LNK-033's invariant and needs its own stopword recalibration against the widened candidate set — the 2026-08-08 calibration deliberately kept 'about' out of LabelStopwords, so '…about your use case' will match an About page the moment About becomes a candidate. That calibration will be redone with a measured report, not assumed.
